sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Plainfield?
sections.html:
Plainfield requires a Certificate of Compliance inspection before a sale closes, and that single step controls your timeline more than any other local rule. A separate fire certificate is also expected, so plan for two inspections that run on different tracks.

Owners here choose between a broker listing, a private sale and an as-is cash purchase. Each route still ends with the same paperwork: the compliance certificate, a recorded deed in Elizabeth, and the state transfer filings.

Plainfield had 57,141 residents in the mid-2025 estimate, and owners live in 44.8 percent of homes, so rentals make up the larger part of the housing stock. The median owned home is valued at $410,800 and median gross rent is $1,767. With 3.41 people per household, many homes serve larger families or hold more than one unit. Buyers and appraisers look closely at legal unit counts, which is one reason the city checks occupancy during a sale inspection.

sections.h2: What the Plainfield Certificate of Compliance covers
sections.html:
You file the Certificate of Compliance for Sale application with the city's Property Maintenance Unit and book an inspection before closing. The form asks about the property's legal occupancy, the buyer, the closing date, permits and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. An LLC seller must add its Certificate of Formation.

Plainfield Certificate of Compliance fees, June 2026 forms
ChargeAmount
First residential unit$50
Each added unit$25
Missed appointment$25
Exemption application$75
Escrow for a temporary certificate$500 per unit

An adult must be present to let the inspector in. Inspectors look at both the structure and the way the property is used:

  • Exterior walls, roofs, porches, stairs, railings and accessory buildings.
  • Yards, driveways, trash, tall vegetation and abandoned vehicles.
  • Kitchens, bathrooms, basements, crawlspaces and bedrooms.
  • Plumbing, hot water, heating equipment, outlets and fixtures.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, windows, doors and floors.
  • Signs of leaks, moisture or vermin, and the legal number of units.
  • Open permits or work that appears to have been done without one.

Other paperwork may be due as well. Sellers can be asked for a heating system certification on a professional's letterhead, a Fire Division certificate for smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and a portable extinguisher, and permit approvals for completed work. A building with three or more units needs a current certificate from the state Bureau of Housing Inspection. Ask the Fire Division for its current fee.

sections.h2: What happens if a Plainfield house fails the inspection?
sections.html:
The owner receives a notice of violation, fixes the items, pulls any missing permits and requests a reinspection. A clear certificate is issued only after that. Most notices allow up to 30 days. Exterior items such as trash and overgrown vegetation can carry a deadline as short as five business days, and an immediate safety threat can require action within three days.

The city may approve a temporary certificate when the property is in substantial compliance. That route requires a $500 per unit escrow, and the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting responsibility for the remaining violations. Approval is discretionary, so do not count on it before you sign a contract.

Some transactions qualify for an exemption, and the city makes the final call after reviewing documents:

  • The construction official issued a certificate of occupancy or continued occupancy within 90 days before the sale.
  • The house is owned by the City of Plainfield.
  • A refinance with no change in ownership.
  • A building officially found unfit for habitation and headed for rehabilitation or demolition.
  • Certain documented foreclosure or short sale closings where the property cannot be reached for inspection.

Begin as soon as a contract names a closing date. Send the Certificate of Compliance for Sale application to the Property Maintenance Unit with the buyer's name, the closing date and your permit details, then book the inspection and arrange for an adult to open the door. Ask the Fire Division about its smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and extinguisher inspection in the same week so the two visits do not collide.

If a notice of violation arrives, read each deadline. Trash and vegetation items can be short, while most others allow up to 30 days. Pull any missing permits, finish the repairs and request the reinspection before your attorney sets the final closing appointment. Without a clear certificate or an approved temporary one, the closing can stall at the Elizabeth recording step.

Plainfield has six residential historic districts, and a few carry real weight with buyers who want large older houses: Van Wyck Brooks, Netherwood Heights, Crescent Area, Hillside Avenue and Sleepy Hollow. If your house sits in one of them, ask the city's planning office whether any exterior repair you plan before listing needs historic review.

sections.h2: Transfer fee and deed recording in Plainfield
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's realty transfer fee. On a sale above $350,000 the schedule runs $2.90 per $500 up to $150,000, $4.25 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $4.80 per $500 from $200,000 to $550,000. The median value of $410,800 sits in that last band.

Your deed goes to the Union County Clerk's recording office at 2 Broad Street in Elizabeth. Weekday hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, counter recording ends at 3:30 pm, and nobody needs an appointment. Deeds over $1,000,000 recorded after July 10, 2025 may carry a revised fee.

Your closing agent normally prepares the deed, the transfer fee affidavit and the Gross Income Tax residency form, and you sign them at the closing table.

sections.h2: Steps to take with tenants in place
sections.html:
If tenants live in the house, a rental unit needs its own Certificate of Compliance whenever the tenant named on the old one leaves. Give the buyer copies of the leases and ask the Property Maintenance Unit whether your rental certificate is current.

For a building with three or more units, confirm the state Bureau of Housing Inspection certificate is up to date before you list. Buyers' attorneys ask for it, and a lapsed certificate can cost you days at the end of the deal.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits a Plainfield owner best?
sections.html:
It depends on repairs, timing and who is living in the house. A listing may reach more buyers, but it brings repair requests, showings and a lender's appraisal, all of which interact with the compliance inspection.

An as-is cash purchase lets you skip the repair list, though the inspection, fire certificate and recording steps still apply. Compare written terms before signing: who orders the compliance application, who carries the $500 escrow if a temporary certificate is used, and who pays the transfer fee.

faqs.q: Is a Certificate of Compliance required when I sell in Plainfield?
faqs.a: Yes. The Property Maintenance Unit asks sellers to file the Certificate of Compliance for Sale application and schedule an inspection before closing. A recent certificate of occupancy issued by the construction official within 90 days can support an exemption request.

faqs.q: How much does the Plainfield sale inspection cost?
faqs.a: The first residential unit costs $50 and each added unit costs $25 on the June 2026 application. A missed appointment adds $25 and an exemption application costs $75. A separate fire certificate fee may apply, so ask the Fire Division for its current charge.

faqs.q: Can I close in Plainfield with violations still open?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The city can issue a temporary Certificate of Compliance when a property is in substantial compliance, but it requires a $500 per unit escrow and a notarized buyer affidavit. The decision is discretionary and does not apply to every violation.

faqs.q: Where is a Plainfield deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Union County Clerk's recording office, 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth. Over the counter recording runs until 3:30 pm on weekdays and needs no appointment. The clerk requires a cover sheet with each land document.

faqs.q: What extra steps apply if my Plainfield house has tenants?
faqs.a: A rental unit needs its own Certificate of Compliance whenever a new tenant moves in, and a building with three or more units needs a current state Bureau of Housing Inspection certificate. Give the buyer copies of the leases and ask the Property Maintenance Unit whether your rental certificate is current.
